bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet; capital allocation prioritized for organic growth and utilization improvement over inorganic M&A; capex disciplined to maximize ROCE; focus on reducing logistics cost via marine fleet (7 vessels ordered) and rail-linked fly ash; no dividend or buyback guidance provided
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Soft demand due to inflation/weak monsoon; inability to pass on INR250/tonne cost increases; delayed railway infrastructure for fly ash; prolonged underperformance of acquired assets (Sanghi, Penna); geopolitical fuel volatility; margin compression from pricing pressure despite cost spikes
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on execution, candid on challenges; acknowledged cost overruns and underperformance of acquired assets; emphasized internal control over external factors; tone shifted from optimism in Q3 to realism in Q4; committed to transparency on stabilization timeline; reiterated 'One Cement' platform as strategic priority
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Orient Cement's integration is complete for financial reporting (PPPA finalized), but operational integration remains incomplete; cost spike in March was not just macro but also due to internal operational delays (maintenance, branding, heat inefficiency); 32% green energy share is already above industry avg and a key margin lever; marine logistics (7 vessels) is a silent capex play replacing rail dependency for Sanghi; INR4,500/tonne cost is a peak, not baseline — management expects sequential decline
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deck's capital-allocation framing is Adani-portfolio level: 'Growth Capital - Platform', 'Infrastructure Financing Framework', 'Duration Risk Matching', 'Diversified Source of Capital'.
- Long-term debt mix shown for Mar'26 across PSU Banks, Pvt. Banks, USD Bonds, DII, Global Int. Banks, NBFCs & FIs and Capex LC (9%, 22%, 22%, 1%, 24%, 3%, 19% as printed).
- Highest AAA / A1+ credit ratings from CRISIL and CARE, with healthy cash flows stated to sustain the capex programme.
- Ambuja consolidated borrowings shown at ₹53 Cr as on 31-Mar-26 against total equity of ₹71,846 Cr; the deck makes no statement on dividends.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Recognised for its focus on durability and sustainability, offering advanced materials positioned for long-lasting and responsible construction
- Access to a structured network of Master Supply Agreements across the Adani Cement portfolio (Ambuja Cements, ACC, Sanghi Industries, Asian Fine Cement, Penna Cement Industries, Adani Cement Industries) enabling reciprocal sourcing, flexible allocation of cement/clinker/fly-ash/coal, shared infrastructure and brand leverage under the procuring entity's brand; sold 6 million tonnes of Cement and Clinker under these arrangements during the year
- Quality assurance framework aligned with parent organisation's operating, quality and sustainability systems, with standardised, certified testing infrastructure across the value chain
- Integrated logistics framework with Driver Management Centres, performance-based logistics scorecards, and a collaboration with Container Corporation of India (CONCOR) to scale up rail-based bulk cement transportation, aimed at lowering transportation costs and carbon intensity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Maintaining market position in a dynamic industry environment — The Indian cement market is evolving rapidly, with consolidation and ongoing capacity additions across the industry increasing competitive pressure on market share and profitability; mitigation rests on the parent's (Ambuja Cements') capacity expansion and OCL's brand-equity building through innovation and digitalisation.
- Compliance with a changing regulatory landscape — Regulatory requirements, particularly climate and environmental standards, are evolving rapidly; non-compliance carries reputational and financial consequences, and adapting (e.g. new emission standards for dust, SOx and NOx under MoEF&CC) can require substantial transformation costs.
- Fuel and raw material security — The cement business is capital-intensive and heavily reliant on energy and resources such as limestone, fly ash and coal, which form a significant share of operating costs, making cost management and supply continuity critical to competitiveness.
- Cybersecurity threats — Growing digital exposure and reliance on AI tools increase the risk of data leakage and threats to information systems, requiring continuous investment in secure, monitored IT/OT environments.
- Health and safety — Cement manufacturing is a high-risk operating environment requiring a multidisciplinary, organisation-wide safety commitment; lapses could result in accidents, requiring continuous review of frontline safety systems and processes.
- Natural resource availability — Heavy reliance on natural resources such as limestone and coal means continuity of supply at optimal cost and quality is critical to smooth operations, requiring resource-efficiency initiatives and long-term mine investments to secure supply.
- Energy security and cost inflation — Energy costs form a significant share of production costs, particularly in the energy-intensive kilning and grinding processes, so fluctuating energy prices directly affect profitability, requiring fuel-source diversification and efficiency initiatives.
- Project execution risk on the group's capacity expansion — Execution is central to the group's vision of reaching 119 MTPA cement capacity by FY 2026-27, with large-scale projects underway at multiple sites; timely completion, safety/quality standards and budget adherence are key execution risks.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Ownership chain as stated: 'Cement includes 67.29% (67.33% on Voting Rights basis) stake in Ambuja Cements Ltd. as on 30th June'26 which in turn owns 50.05% in ACC Limited. Adani directly owns 6.64% stake in ACC Limited & Ambuja Cements Ltd. holds 72.66% stake in Orient Cement Ltd.'
- Orient's Chittapur, Jalgaon and Devapur plants are shown on the group's 'PAN India Presence' map alongside Ambuja and ACC units; group presence is stated as '31 states & union territories and 665+ districts'.
- Group-level scale for the quarter ended June 30, 2026: 109 MTPA cement capacity, 24 integrated units, 22 grinding units, 119 ready-mix concrete plants, 10 bulk cement terminals, 11 captive ships and '1,25,000+ channel partners across India'.
- Strategy framed as 'Focus on value over volumes, trade and premium products', a 'Hyperlocal and Segmented Sales strategy basis market share and contribution', and an AI-enabled sales and logistics operating model.
- Deck lists 'Balance Sheet Strength' as a key investment highlight: 'Highest AAA / A1+ credit ratings from CRISIL and CARE.'
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Ticker vs deck] The cover letter is Orient Cement Limited's Reg-30 filing (Scrip 535754 / ORIENTCEM), but the presentation itself is Ambuja Cements Limited's Q1 FY2027 deck; essentially all operating, cost, ESG and financial data are Ambuja consolidated/standalone or Adani-portfolio figures, not Orient Cement figures.
- [Mergers] 'reversal of tax provisions ... primarily on account of the mergers of Sanghi (wef 1st April 2024), and Penna (wef 16th August 2024), both of which have now been successfully completed', giving tax shields from unabsorbed depreciation and accumulated losses; overall one-time benefit in FY26 consolidated financials of approximately Rs 1,365 Cr.
- [Group financing] 'AEL has raised INR 15,000 Cr through Qualified Institutional Placement ('QIP') during July'26. Accordingly, promoter's shareholding stands revised to 71.97%.'
- [Industry outlook - CRISIL] 'Cement demand likely to stay soft at ~5% in FY27 amid headwinds, while secular demand long-term story remains intact'; segment split Housing 55%, Infrastructure 30%, commercial 15%; industry capacity/demand shown as 411/271 (FY15), 751/474 (FY26E) and 958/621 (FY30E) MT.
- [Restructuring] Ambuja standalone previous periods 'have been restated on account of merger of Sanghi & Penna with Ambuja'.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Orient Cement Limited manufactures and sells cement and clinker (100% of turnover) through modern cement manufacturing plants and a dedicated clinker grinding unit, serving individual home-builders, developers, infrastructure projects, masons, contractors and professionals across 12 states and 115 districts in India, with no exports. Following Ambuja Cements' acquisition of control during FY 2025-26, the Company now operates within the Adani Group's 'One Cement Platform', drawing on Master Supply Agreements with group cement entities for the structured movement of cement, clinker and other materials.

latest_quarter.body: FY26 avg cost: INR4,400/tonne (vs target INR4,000); Q4 cost: INR4,500/tonne (INR250/tonne spike from West Asia war, packing bags, fuel); normalized cost: INR4,250/tonne; key cost drivers: higher freight (increased lead distance), packing (INR25/bag spike), branding (trade sales push), heat consumption (35-40 kcal higher), lower government incentives (GST changes); expected savings: INR150-200/tonne from fly ash (railway infra pending) and green energy (32% share in Q4)

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 10M tonnes new capacity (GU/clinker) to commission by Sept '26; Mundra (new clinker line) and Assam (limestone block) greenfield projects in pipeline; potential for incremental volume from improved utilization of 19M tonnes acquired capacity (Sanghi+Penna); long-term capacity target of 119M tonnes by FY27, with FY28+ capex deferred to optimize existing assets
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- 'Accelerating Infrastructure, Leveraging Intelligence' — strengthening capabilities through integration of digital platforms and AI-enabled analytics across operations, planning and market execution to enhance visibility, decision-making and reliability
- Integration into Ambuja Cements' 'One Cement Platform' to access scale, legacy, technical depth and digital execution capabilities, aligned with a long-term growth blueprint built on disciplined capital allocation, digital integration and sustainability leadership
- Building a simpler, flatter, more empowered organisational structure with district-level ownership models and digitally enabled execution frameworks, shifting from volume push to value-driven demand pull
- Continued focus on cost optimisation, operational efficiency and disciplined capital allocation amid cost pressures from global energy markets, logistics constraints and currency movements
- Advancing alternative energy initiatives (renewable power, AFR utilisation in captive power plant and kilns) to reduce reliance on finite resources and partially mitigate EBITDA impact
- RESQ focus — Reliability, Environment, Safety and Quality — including industry-first safety innovations (drone-led inspections, automated sampling, AI-enabled monitoring), structured shutdown governance and a Zero Harm safety culture
- Sustainability commitments as capital-allocation levers: expansion of renewable energy capacity, integration of waste heat recovery systems, increased alternative fuels and raw materials use, higher blended cement ratios, advancement of carbon capture and utilisation pilots, and circular waste management through Geoclean
- Investment in talent and culture — capability building, digital upskilling and leadership development via platforms such as Adani Cement FutureX and industry partnerships, viewed as integral to successful integration
- The Company has consistently declared dividends since inception, guided by its Dividend Distribution and Shareholder Return Policy adopted under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations (available on the Company's website). No amount was transferred to General Reserves during the year, with retained earnings carried forward on the balance sheet.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: OCL's own manufacturing network stands at 8.5 MTPA. Growth is being pursued organically through higher capacity optimisation and deeper penetration in core markets, supported by improved logistics and integration with the group's distribution networks ('Accelerating Growth' pillar), with progress noted as improved capacity-utilisation levels, an expanded dealer network across key regions, and enhanced dispatch efficiencies through supply-chain optimisation. At the group level, Adani Cement's 'One Cement Platform' — consolidating ACC, Orient Cement, Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement Industries under Ambuja Cements — targets cement manufacturing capacity expansion from ~109 MTPA to 119 MTPA by FY 2026-27 in a structured, phased manner. The Company also directs R&D and capex toward improving the environmental and social impact of products and processes, including new product development with lower clinker usage, studies on calcined clay, enhanced use of alternative materials, and lowering heat of hydration.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Company anticipates cement demand in India will expand by approximately 5% in FY 2026-27, following a robust 6.5-7.5% growth phase in FY 2025-26 fuelled by housing and infrastructure momentum
- India's per-capita cement consumption (~290 kg) remains well below the global average (~540 kg), signalling long-term headroom as urbanisation, household formation and formalisation of housing continue
- Government infrastructure push — the $2.6 trillion National Infrastructure Pipeline, PLI scheme, Smart Cities initiatives, sustained FDI inflows and China+1-led manufacturing shifts — expected to underpin infrastructure-led cement demand
- A potential reduction in the GST rate for cement is anticipated to sustain demand momentum into FY 2026-27; the GST rate on cement was already reduced from 28% to 18% during the year, reshaping affordability and stimulating consumption
- Input cost pressures — fuel, logistics, energy, coal, petcoke, freight and a depreciating Rupee on imported resources — continue to weigh on industry profitability, requiring disciplined execution and cost management
- Industry capacity additions are projected at 42-44 MTPA in FY 2026-27, following additions of 50-55 MTPA in FY 2025-26; capacity utilisation expected to stay broadly stable around 70-71%, with the southern region (a key OCL market) likely to see comparatively moderate utilisation due to capacity overhang
- Structural enablers — improving rail connectivity, port infrastructure and coastal shipping reducing freight costs, alongside rising adoption of blended/low-carbon cements, green building standards, digitisation and precast/modular construction — are reshaping demand toward more sustainable, efficient building solutions
- Continuing emphasis on renewable power, AFR utilisation in captive power plant and kilns, operational efficiency, digitalisation and prudent control of discretionary spending helped partially mitigate cost pressure on EBITDA
- Balance sheet has continued to be managed effectively and is now nearly net debt-free
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Ambuja's consolidated FY26 performance was driven by record volumes and premiumization, but margins were pressured by acquired asset inefficiencies, fuel/packaging cost spikes, and delayed capex benefits; FY27 focus is on stabilizing Sanghi/Penna/Orient assets to unlock 5-10% utilization gains and achieve INR150-200/tonne cost savings via fly ash and green energy.
